title: Design System: Clarkson Formula Electric Knights

display.purpose: Hero H1, subteam-page H1, section headings, card titles. Always uppercase Oswald.

body.purpose: Hero paragraph, placeholder body copy. Always sentence case.

label.purpose: Nav links, spec-code chips, figure numbers, footer. The one place uppercase is earned.

caption.purpose: Media-plate figure captions and sponsor names. Mono, but sentence/mixed case — a caption is a sentence and a sponsor name is set the way its owner sets it.

shadows.name: hazard-tag
shadows.purpose: Under the diagonal hazard-tag ribbon only, since it reads as a physically bolted-on object.

shadows.name: sponsor-halo
shadows.value: drop-shadow(0 0 1px rgba(243,240,230,1)) drop-shadow(0 0 3px rgba(243,240,230,0.7)) drop-shadow(0 0 12px rgba(243,240,230,0.28))
shadows.purpose: Backlight for dark sponsor artwork on Chassis Ink. Zero offset, so it is light and not elevation; drop-shadow traces the logo's alpha channel so the halo follows the letterforms, not a rectangle.

shadows.name: sponsor-halo-hover
shadows.value: drop-shadow(0 0 1px rgba(243,240,230,1)) drop-shadow(0 0 4px rgba(243,240,230,0.8)) drop-shadow(0 0 16px rgba(255,205,0,0.45))
shadows.purpose: Sponsor halo on hover: the outermost pass warms to Hazard Gold.

motion.name: ease-entrance
motion.purpose: Hero frame/crosshair/hazard-tag entrance and card reveal.

components.name: Spec Plate Card
components.description: One subteam per card: rivet-dot corners, a gold-on-black spec-code chip, a dot-grid 'photo pending' plate, and a stenciled uppercase title.

components.css: .ds-card { position: relative; display: block; background: #101c17; border: 1px solid rgba(226,232,227,0.14); text-decoration: none; color: inherit; background-image: radial-gradient(circle at 10px 10px, rgba(226,232,227,0.4) 1.6px, transparent 2px), radial-gradient(circle at calc(100% - 10px) 10px, rgba(226,232,227,0.4) 1.6px, transparent 2px), radial-gradient(circle at 10px calc(100% - 10px), rgba(226,232,227,0.4) 1.6px, transparent 2px), radial-gradient(circle at calc(100% - 10px) calc(100% - 10px), rgba(226,232,227,0.4) 1.6px, transparent 2px); transition: transform 0.2s ease, border-color 0.2s ease; } .ds-card:hover { transform: translateY(-4px); border-color: #ffcd00; } .ds-card-code { position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.68rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.05em; color: #ffcd00; background: rgba(5,5,5,0.75); padding: 3px 9px 3px 7px; border-bottom-right-radius: 3px; } .ds-card:hover .ds-card-code { background: #ffcd00; color: #050505; } .ds-card-plate { aspect-ratio: 16/9; width: 100%; background-image: radial-gradient(circle, rgba(226,232,227,0.14) 1px, transparent 1.4px); background-size: 16px 16px; background-color: #142620; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; color: #b3c7b9; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.78rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.08em; } .ds-card-title { font-family: Oswald, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.02em; margin: 0; padding: 1rem 1.1rem; font-size: 1.05rem; color: #f3f0e6; }

components.name: Back Button
components.description: Ruled-border text button, mono uppercase, gold on hover/focus.
components.css: .ds-btn-back { display: inline-block; padding: 0.6rem 1.2rem; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.8rem; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; border: 1px solid rgba(226,232,227,0.32); color: #f3f0e6; text-decoration: none; transition: border-color 0.2s ease, color 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-back:hover, .ds-btn-back:focus-visible { border-color: #ffcd00; color: #ffcd00; }

components.name: Hazard Tag
components.description: Diagonal ribbon fixed to the hero's top-right corner: gold fill, repeating black-stripe trim, short mono caution label. The system's signature component.
components.css: .ds-hazard-tag { position: relative; width: 260px; padding: 9px 0; background: #ffcd00; transform: rotate(45deg); box-shadow: 0 6px 18px rgba(0,0,0,0.45); } .ds-hazard-tag::before, .ds-hazard-tag::after { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; height: 6px; background: repeating-linear-gradient(-45deg, #050505 0 8px, transparent 8px 16px); } .ds-hazard-tag::before { top: 0; } .ds-hazard-tag::after { bottom: 0; } .ds-hazard-tag span { display: block; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.68rem; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #050505; text-align: center; }

components.name: Lead Card
components.description: A spec plate for a person: same Panel ground, rivet-dot corners, LD·NN spec code and gold hover as the subteam card, but a 4:5 portrait well instead of 16:9 and a stacked caption — name in Oswald uppercase over the subteam as a mono spec label. Officers add a warm-white .lead-role line (Captain, Chief Engineer) between the name and the subteam; every card stays the same size, with .lead-caption min-height reserving the role line's space on the cards that lack one. Links to a lead detail page (portrait left, bio right).

components.name: Media Plate
components.description: Every real photograph is mounted as a figure: Panel ground, hairline border, rivet-dot corners, and a mono caption opening with a gold Fig. NN number. Variants: --crop (16:9 object-fit band, with .crop-upper/.crop-mid to shift it per photo) and --cutout.
components.css: .ds-media-plate { position: relative; margin: 2rem 0 0; padding: 0; border: 1px solid rgba(226,232,227,0.14); background: #101c17; background-image: radial-gradient(circle at 10px 10px, rgba(226,232,227,0.4) 1.6px, transparent 2px), radial-gradient(circle at calc(100% - 10px) 10px, rgba(226,232,227,0.4) 1.6px, transparent 2px), radial-gradient(circle at 10px calc(100% - 10px), rgba(226,232,227,0.4) 1.6px, transparent 2px), radial-gradient(circle at calc(100% - 10px) calc(100% - 10px), rgba(226,232,227,0.4) 1.6px, transparent 2px); } .ds-media-plate img { display: block; width: 100%; height: auto; } .ds-media-plate figcaption { padding: 0.7rem 1rem; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.8rem; line-height: 1.5; color: #b3c7b9; border-top: 1px solid rgba(226,232,227,0.14); } .ds-fig-number { color: #ffcd00; font-weight: 600; margin-right: 0.4em; }

components.name: Sponsor Logo
components.description: A sponsor link: an invisible 3:2 frame over a mono name line. Plate width (--lg/--md/--sm) is the only signal of support level, and the levels are never named on the page or in the class names. Dark foreign artwork is backlit by three zero-offset drop-shadow passes tracing its alpha channel rather than boxed on a white plate; hover warms the outermost pass to gold and lifts the unit 3px.
components.html: Altium
components.css: .ds-sponsor { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 0.7rem; text-decoration: none; transition: transform 0.2s ease; } .ds-sponsor:hover { transform: translateY(-3px); } .ds-sponsor--lg { width: clamp(9rem, 21vw, 16.25rem); } .ds-sponsor--md { width: clamp(7.25rem, 16vw, 12.5rem); } .ds-sponsor--sm { width: clamp(6rem, 13vw, 10.25rem); } .ds-sponsor-mark { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 3 / 2; min-height: 0; padding: 0.8rem; } .ds-sponsor-mark img { display: block; width: 100%; height: 100%; object-fit: contain; filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1px rgba(243,240,230,1)) drop-shadow(0 0 3px rgba(243,240,230,0.7)) drop-shadow(0 0 12px rgba(243,240,230,0.28)); transition: filter 0.2s ease; } .ds-sponsor:hover .ds-sponsor-mark img { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1px rgba(243,240,230,1)) drop-shadow(0 0 4px rgba(243,240,230,0.8)) drop-shadow(0 0 16px rgba(255,205,0,0.45)); } .ds-sponsor-name { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.72rem; line-height: 1.35; min-height: 2.7em; letter-spacing: 0.04em; color: #b3c7b9; text-align: center; transition: color 0.2s ease; } .ds-sponsor:hover .ds-sponsor-name { color: #ffcd00; }

narrative.overview:
The site reads as a working engineering document that got a warning placard bolted onto it — a real spec sheet, not a marketing template. It refuses the generic dark SaaS-gradient-hero-over-glass-cards arrangement that AI-generated interfaces default to by borrowing its material world from two real things a Formula SAE Electric team actually handles: OSHA-style high-voltage warning signage and technical blueprint drafting. Ground is near-black chassis ink, not a flat neutral; Clarkson green carries structural bands; Clarkson gold is promoted to a real hazard-stripe accent doing visible work rather than a soft hover tint.

The system is deliberately flat and line-drawn rather than soft and glassy: ruled borders, corner registration crosshairs, rivet-dot corners, and diagonal hazard-tape trim carry the texture that gradients and blur would otherwise be reached for.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black chassis-dark ground with the two Clarkson greens doing structural work, gold reserved for real hazard/accent duty.
Flat, line-drawn depth (ruled borders, crosshairs, rivets) — no glass, no soft shadows standing in for structure.
Condensed stenciled display type (Oswald) paired with a signage-lineage body face (Barlow) and a narrowly-scoped mono (IBM Plex Mono) for spec/dimension labels only.
Every subteam is a numbered 'spec plate,' not a generic icon card.

rules.name: The Two-Green Rule
rules.body: Structural bands (the solid header, footer border, subteam-page hero gradient) use only Clarkson Green and Clarkson Green Dark — never a third arbitrary dark neutral invented for convenience.

rules.name: The Hazard Accent Rule
rules.body: Gold only appears as a real hazard/accent device — a ribbon, a spec-code chip, a hover state, an emphasized word — never as a decorative gradient or a low-opacity tint standing in for 'brand color.'

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Body Rule
rules.body: Any text long enough to be a sentence stays in sentence case even when set in the mono label font. Uppercase is reserved for labels under roughly a phrase in length.

rules.name: The Flat Plate Rule
rules.body: Cards, panels, and media plates sit flush with their background at rest — no ambient shadow. The only motion is a hairline border brightening to gold and a slight lift on hover.

rules.name: The Backlight-Not-Box Rule
rules.body: When a foreign asset (a sponsor's logo) is too dark to survive on Chassis Ink, light it from behind with alpha-tracing drop-shadow passes — never box it on a white plate. A white rectangle would put a non-system surface on the page and flatten every sponsor's mark into the same card; the halo keeps each mark's own artwork and transparency intact.

dos: Do keep gold's use rare and load-bearing (ribbon, spec codes, hover, one emphasized headline word) — its rarity is what makes it read as a hazard color rather than a brand tint.
Do use Oswald uppercase for anything that is a label or a heading; use Barlow sentence-case for anything a visitor reads as a sentence.
Do keep new components square-cornered and line-drawn (rivets, crosshairs, hairline borders) rather than reaching for radius + shadow.
Do reuse the spec-code convention (XX·NN) for any new numbered/tagged item.
Do mount every real photograph in a media plate with a numbered Fig. NN caption — a photo is evidence in this world, and evidence is captioned.
Do let foreign artwork (sponsor logos) keep its own colors and transparency; size and a backlight are the only things the system imposes on it.
donts: Don't add glass/blur panels or soft glowing shadows — this world is flat and ruled, not glassy. The sponsor halo is the one exception and stays scoped to sponsor logos: zero offset (backlight, not elevation), and only because foreign dark artwork can't be recolored to suit the ground.
Don't put sponsor logos on white plates or name the support levels in the markup or on the page — plate width is the entire ranking device.
Don't introduce a third dark neutral for backgrounds.
Don't set long-form body copy in uppercase, even in the mono label font.
Don't use repeating-stripe gradients as generic surface decoration; the diagonal hazard-stripe trim is earned specifically because it depicts real hazard tape.
